title: Bulk-Defect Correspondence in Algebraic Classical Spin Liquids
abstract: Local constraints in algebraic classical spin liquids give rise to singular momentum-space correlations. This so called pinch-point singularity carries a momentum-space winding number that determines the low-energy structure of the algebraic spin liquid. We show that nonmagnetic vacancies in two dimensions reveal this topological invariant in the real-space winding of the surrounding spin textures. Under explicit conditions, we prove this bulk-defect correspondence for rank-$n$ $\mathrm{U}(1)$ spin liquids and verify it numerically for the Coulomb spin liquids of the kagome and checkerboard lattices and the rank-2 $\mathrm{U}(1)$ spin liquid of the honeycomb-snowflake model. In this way we show that vacancies can be used as general probes for distinguishing the emergent gauge theories of strongly correlated classical disordered magnets.
summary: This work establishes a rigorous bulk-defect correspondence in algebraic classical spin liquids, showing that a topological invariant calculated from momentum-space singularities matches the winding number measured around a physical vacancy defect. By verifying this for various lattice models, the authors demonstrate that defects serve as universal probes to characterize the emergent gauge theories governing these strongly correlated magnetic materials.
main_problem: The paper establishes a bulk-defect correspondence, linking a topological invariant (winding number) calculated in momentum space to the winding number observed in real space around a local defect (vacancy) in algebraic classical spin liquids.
main_result: The correspondence $W_{	ext{defect}} = W_{	ext{bulk}}$ is proven and numerically verified for rank-n U(1) spin liquids, demonstrating that vacancies act as general probes for distinguishing emergent gauge theories.
method: The analysis uses the constrainer formalism and hybrid field theory (SCGA) to calculate topological invariants in both momentum space (pinch-point singularity) and real space (orphan spin texture).
model_or_system: The study focuses on Algebraic Classical Spin Liquids (CSL) characterized by local constraints, tested on lattices like Kagome and Checkerboard, and generalized to rank-n U(1) models.
key_observables: Winding number ($W$), pinch-point singularity, real-space spin texture winding, enclosed gauge charge ($Q_{	ext{enc}}$), and screening lengths ($\xi$).
important_parameters: Rank of the U(1) symmetry (rank-1 and rank-2), temperature ($T/J$), and lattice geometry (Kagome, Checkerboard, Honeycomb-snowflake).
main_assumptions: The correspondence is proven under explicit conditions, and the analysis relies on continuum field theory approximations and the SCGA framework.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the correspondence by comparing the momentum-space pinch point winding ($W_{	ext{bulk}}$) with the real-space spin texture winding ($W_{	ext{defect}}$) around a vacancy, showing agreement for different ranks.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by defining the bulk invariant from momentum-space constraints, then introduces the defect via vacancies, derives the real-space correlation functions using Lagrange multipliers, and finally proves and verifies the equality of the topological invariants across different lattice models.
why_interesting: The concept of using local defects to probe global topological properties (like gauge fluxes) is a powerful theoretical tool applicable to understanding emergent order in complex many-body systems, relevant to quantum simulation and topological phases.
